measurements_run: Re-ran the reviewer's W1-4b probe with a real pinned SDK (supabase/supabase_auth 2.31.0, httpx 0.28.1) against a ThreadingHTTPServer fake gotrue on 127.0.0.1, through the real /auth/refresh route. 11 real outage shapes plus the real hang all return 401 today. 504, connection refused and reset return 503.

SDK source read on the venv. handle_exception types 502/503/504/520-524/530 as AuthRetryableError. JSON bodies for other statuses become AuthApiError(.status). A non-JSON 4xx/5xx body (HTML 429/500) becomes AuthUnknownError, which has NO .status attribute; its .original_error is the HTTPStatusError. gotrue_base_api._request only catches HTTPStatusError and RuntimeError, so httpx.TransportError escapes unwrapped. The default gotrue httpx timeout is 5.0 s on the flag-OFF branch.

W1-4c measured through threading.enumerate(). refresh_session and login_user each leave one supabase_auth Timer (~3589 s) on both get_auth_client branches. Behavioural: with expires_in=12 the server sends unsolicited POST /token for RT-ISSUED-1 (the device's token) and then RT-ISSUED-2. Flag-ON logout with /logout dropped: RemoteProtocolError is not AuthApiError, so SyncGoTrueClient.sign_out's suppress() does not catch it, _remove_session never runs, and the Timer survives.

Measured an SDK trap: SyncClientOptions.replace(auto_refresh_token=False) cannot disable auto-refresh, because its body is `auto_refresh_token or self.auto_refresh_token`. persist_session behaves the same way. The green phase must use the constructor or set the attributes directly. This is recorded in the W1-4 file docstring.

persist_session=False keeps the set_session plus sign_out logout path working: get_session() returns _in_memory_session, which _save_session stores. So W1-4c does not break the current flag-ON logout path.

Flake found and fixed while writing the test. With expires_in=11, the fake's int(time) against the SDK's round(time) can make expire_in come out as 10. The SDK then uses a 0.5 s margin and arms the Timer at 9.5 s instead of 1 s. The first run was falsely green for that reason. expires_in=12 with a 4 s poll arms at 1-2 s and was red on every later run.

Minor-defect probe: flag ON with no, empty or null refresh token sends zero upstream requests today. Flag ON with a refresh token sends GET /user and then POST /logout?scope=local with Bearer <access>; the refresh-token value never appears on /logout. Flag OFF sends zero requests.

Checked the upstash-redis 1.7.0 API on the venv. It has Redis.set(key, value, nx, xx, get, ex, px, exat, pxat, keepttl), expire(key, seconds, nx, xx, gt, lt), ttl, pttl, eval, pipeline() and multi(), where multi() is a Pipeline posting to /multi-exec with exec(). SET with NX returns format_set -> res == 'OK', so False when the key is not set; EXPIRE returns bool. Both SET NX EX + INCR and a MULTI pipeline are available.

Re-ran the reviewer's W1-9 repro with an in-memory Upstash fake: first expire() raising gives [401x5, 429x2] with no Retry-After, ttl -1, count 5. Added two further shapes: INCR applied but timed out on the client gives ttl -1, and two failure bursts 2 h apart combine into a lock. Also measured that a TTL of -2/-1/0 each gives a windowless ACCOUNT_LOCKED 429 on login, PUT /email and PUT /password.

spec_disagreements: CONFLICT WITH AN EXISTING PIN (the orchestrator must rule at green). tests/test_auth_refresh_and_revocation.py::test_node5_flag_on_without_refresh_token_is_todays_path asserts that flag ON with no refresh token makes exactly a bare sign_out() per logout (['sign_out','sign_out']) and never touches set_session. The W1-4 server-minor ruling (admin.sign_out(access_token,'local') regardless of refresh token) necessarily breaks it: its stub StubGoTrueAuth has no .admin, so the green path would raise AttributeError, the broad except would swallow it, and the call log would be empty. Nodes 3 and 4 in that file pin the set_session-then-sign_out ORDER and will also need rewriting if the green calls admin.sign_out directly. My new tests are written against the upstream wire (POST /logout?scope=local, Bearer access) and do not care whether set_session is used.

Reviewer's severity list for W1-4b is correct. It is also incomplete: HTML-body 429 and 500 responses (gateway or Cloudflare error pages) come out of the SDK as AuthUnknownError, not AuthApiError, and carry no .status. The reviewer's proposed predicate (AuthRetryableError | httpx.TransportError | AuthApiError with status 429 or >=500) would leave those two shapes at 401. They are included as RED rows (429_html, 500_html). The green needs to inspect AuthUnknownError.original_error (an httpx.HTTPStatusError) or the equivalent.

The reviewer describes the 504 and connection-reset shapes as already 503. Measured true on Windows, for both the WinError 10054 and the Linux Errno 104 reset messages. Only substring luck ('Gateway Timeout' contains 'timeout'; 'Connection' appears in both reset messages) makes them work, so they are pinned as must-stay-503.

The reviewer's behavioural W1-4c probe (expires_in=12, 'about 18 POSTs in 9 s') is reproducible. An expires_in of 11 is not reliable, because of the SDK's round() against the server's int() on expires_at (measured as a false green once). The test uses 12.

W1-9 defect 3 (Redis TTL rounding against slowapi's +1) was reproduced:false by the reviewer and is outside the ruling. I did not pin a rounding rule. I did add RED nodes for the ruling's clause that the lockout 429 'carries a real retry_after': TTL -2 or 0 after GET says locked must either let the caller through or carry a positive window. Today both give a windowless 429. Descope these two nodes (test_w1_9b_locked_429_is_never_windowless[-2/0]) if the orchestrator reads the ruling as covering TTL -1 only.

Out of this group's ruling, so no tests were written: W1-9 defect 2 (SlowAPIMiddleware discards the async handler under ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS; it lives in app/main.py); W1-4 server defect 3 (logout 422s non-JSON bodies and skips the blacklist); W1-4 client defect 1 (an expired Bearer 401s before logout_user runs); W1-4 client defect 3 (the flag-ON logout makes sync upstream calls on the event loop, and the ruling says nothing about offloading). W1-4 server defect 4 (scrub mutations M7 and M9) is tests-only, so I added both pins; they are green today.

The reviewer's W1-4c fix proposes merging into build_supabase_client_options(). That builder is shared with database_service's admin and user-scoped clients, and SyncClientOptions.replace() cannot set False. Changing the builder would therefore affect callers outside the ruling ('both branches of get_auth_client'). I pinned nothing on the other callers' options, but the green should construct the anon options locally rather than change the shared builder.

Scope pin: the W1-4b ruling covers the refresh path only. I pinned login_user, register_user, request_password_reset and sign_in_with_social to their exact current result dicts for the same transient exceptions (for example AuthRetryableError 503 from login still returns 'Something went wrong. Please try again later.'). A green that widens type classification to every caller of _categorize_auth_error will turn those pins red. That is intentional and needs a separate ruling if wanted.
